label: D2 after a rare a2->S1 transition (chose a2, landed in S1)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (the step where the reached state is shown), almost exclusively when the agent chose a2 and the rare transition took it to S1 (in_action=2, in_state=1): 97% of activation mass is on that conjunction. It is silent at D1 and GO, and close to silent on the common a1->S1 transition (3% of mass, small activations) and on any S2 arrival. The bare rare a2->S1 predicate gets F1 0.79 (precision 0.70, mass recall 0.97). Most false positives come late in the episode, where firing fades: the rate drops steadily with trial number and is near zero by trials 90-99. Late in the episode it keeps firing when the previous trial was unrewarded (D1 showed r0). Adding (prev_reward==0 | ep_trial<60) lifts F1 to 0.89 on dev with mass recall 0.96. Magnitude is larger when the previous trial was unrewarded (that clause holds 63% of mass but only 41% of active steps). Every variable used is observed by D2.

issues: The core claims hold up. On dev the feature fires only at D2: D1 and GO have 0 active steps, and D2 holds 100% of activation mass. in_action=2 holds 96.9% of mass and in_state=1 holds 99.7%. a1->S1 (common) gets 3.1% of mass with precision 0.02. S2 arrivals get 0.3% of mass. The bare rare a2->S1 predicate scores dev F1 0.787 (test 0.781), with mass recall 0.966. Firing falls off with trial number: precision is 0.98 for trials <30, 0.95 for 30-59, 0.41 for 60-89 and 0.04 for 90+. prev_reward==0 gets 63% of mass on 36% of the predicted steps.

Systematic false-positive class: the predicate's (prev_reward==0) branch has no upper bound on trial number, but the feature is silent at trials 90-99 even when the previous trial was unrewarded. B & (ep_trial>=90) & (prev_reward==0) has dev precision 0.11 on 1900 predicted steps, about 45% of the predicate's roughly 4000 dev false positives. That clause catches about 0.1% of activation mass. So the explanation's claim that late in the episode the feature 'keeps firing when the previous trial was unrewarded' is only true up to about trial 85-90. It also contradicts the explanation's own statement that firing is near zero at trials 90-99.

The unrewarded-history effect fades gradually rather than at one cutoff. With prev_reward==0, precision is 0.96 at trials 60-74, 0.77 at 75-89 and 0.11 at 90+. With prev_reward==1, precision is 0.92 at 45-59 and 0.29 at 60-74. So ep_trial<60 is a rough approximation of a decay with trial number, and the decay comes later after unrewarded trials.

The remaining misses (test: 6503 steps, 4.2% of mass) are scattered and low-magnitude. They are mostly rare a2->S1 arrivals late in the episode after a rewarded trial, plus faint firing on other D2 steps. They do not form a meaningful missed class.
No future variables are used. The 'uses future variables: false' claim is correct.
